title: recognizePage
body:
## recognizePage

Recognize the text of one scanned-page PNG with Tesseract 5.5.3 and a pinned English LSTM model, then publish a checked machine draft: page text, every word's box in source pixels with the recogniser's uncalibrated confidence, and a summary that binds the exact image, model, settings and runtime. Use it when a page exists only as pixels, for example a scan or a rendered PDF page; MuPDF text extraction does not read pixels. Choose pageSegmentation to match the layout, optionally declare a dpi and the MuPDF origin. The native TSV is re-read by an independent strict reader and the text must agree with it, but nothing here shows that the text is what the page says: a person must review it. Handwriting, other languages, multipage files, columns and tables, and any claim of accuracy or accessibility are outside this route.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Confidence is the recogniser's own 0-100 score, not accuracy or a probability.
- A successful run proves consistency with the recorded native run, not truth.
- The image identifies pixels only; page identity comes only from a matching declared origin.

Native binding: `tesseract captured-page.png native --tessdata-dir tessdata -l eng --oem 1 --psm PSM [--dpi DPI] -c tessedit_create_txt=1 -c tessedit_create_tsv=1`. Output kind: `["text"]`.

Inputs: none.

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `image` | The scanned page as an object: an absolute local PNG path and an optional SHA-256 pin. In a workflow this path can be the image artifact of an earlier verified step, for example a rendered PDF page. Only the pixels are read; the route cannot know which document or page they came from unless an origin is declared. | `{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":4096,"required":true},"sha256":{"type":"string","minLength":64,"maxLength":64}}}` | **required** |
| `model` | The recognition model as an object: an absolute local English traineddata path and its required SHA-256. The file is streamed into the run, hashed before and after, and the run uses that retained copy; no global tessdata directory, TESSDATA_PREFIX or download is involved. | `{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":4096,"required":true},"sha256":{"type":"string","minLength":64,"maxLength":64,"required":true}}}` | **required** |
| `origin` | Optional declaration of where the page image came from. It currently supports a MuPDF review summary: the route checks that the declared page entry has the same width, height and RGB-pixel SHA-256 as the image, then records the PDF digest and page number. Without it the result states the origin is unknown. It does not re-verify the MuPDF run. | `{"type":"object","properties":{"kind":{"type":"enum","values":["mupdf-review"],"required":true},"summary":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":4096,"required":true},"page":{"type":"integer","minimum":1,"maximum":128,"required":true}}}` | omitted |
| `language` | Recognition language. Only eng (English) is offered, passed to Tesseract as -l eng; omitting it means eng. The name selects the model file by name only; the route does not check that the pinned model is English. Other languages, mixed-language and script detection are outside this route. | `{"type":"enum","values":["eng"]}` | `"eng"` |
| `pageSegmentation` | How Tesseract should treat the page layout. uniform-block assumes a single block of text lines (--psm 6); single-line assumes exactly one line (--psm 7). Neither is a layout analysis: a mismatched choice can return no words or wrong text, and the wrong text is published like any other draft. On the qualification fixture, single-line on a two-line page returned no words and the run failed with OCR_NO_TEXT instead of publishing an empty draft; that was observed on one fixture and does not mean a wrong choice is always caught. | `{"type":"enum","values":["uniform-block","single-line"]}` | `"uniform-block"` |
| `dpi` | Optional declared scan density in dots per inch (70-2400) passed to Tesseract as --dpi. Omit it to use the density stored in the PNG, or Tesseract's own estimate when there is none. Schemaxis does not resample the file, but Tesseract may use the declared density in its size and layout heuristics, so declaring a density the page does not have can change recognition. It is unrelated to the pixel budget: the image must still fit in 4,194,304 pixels, whatever density is declared, so dpi cannot make a large page acceptable. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":70,"maximum":2400}` | omitted |
